map.summary: The answers subsystem defines application-owned async provider contracts for embeddings, generation, and reranking with strict validating dataclasses and content-addressed chunk identity. Cohere adapters (opt-in) and deterministic fake adapters both implement these contracts; live adapters sanitize SDK failures into ProviderError codes and derive Decimal cost/latency usage, while fakes report zero cost and stable synthetic outputs.
unknowns: No caller wiring is shown selecting between fake and Cohere providers; whether configured_* factories are invoked at runtime is uncertain (F0031).
Whether generation temperature/timeout validation and rerank cost fields are exercised by an orchestration layer is not evidenced (F0032).
No CLI, HTTP endpoint, or UI appears in these findings, so no user-facing flow can be described.
Where ChunkingConfig, Chunk, and tokenizer provisioning are consumed by indexing or other pipeline stages is not shown.
SDK client lifetime is owned by callers, but which caller constructs and closes the Cohere AsyncClientV2 outside the open_* factories is not evidenced.

diagrams.title: Architecture
diagrams.description: Shared protocol contracts are implemented by both the opt-in Cohere live adapters and the deterministic fake family; usage/cost and ProviderError are cross-cutting. The configured_* factories are the boundary callers would use, but caller wiring is not evidenced.

diagrams.title: Chunk identity
diagrams.description: ChunkingConfig normalizes into a canonical version digest, and chunk content plus canonicalized sorted source spans feed a content-addressed chunk_id; the boundary matters because identity is derived, never stored.

diagrams.title: Generation request lifecycle
diagrams.description: A validated GenerationRequest is sent as a non-streaming chat with a hard timeout and no SDK retries, then strictly parsed into a GenerationResult carrying Decimal cost and latency; failures become mapped ProviderErrors.

diagrams.title: Reranking boundary
diagrams.description: RerankRequest enforces unique candidate IDs and top_n bounds before any call; the Cohere adapter validates returned count, index uniqueness, and descending scores, mapping indexes back to candidate IDs with cost from billed search units.

diagrams.title: Tokenizer provisioning
diagrams.description: Checksum-pinned tokenizer assets bind model, revision, and sha256; provisioning verifies existing files, atomically publishes fetched files, and rejects settings whose model is unsupported. TextTokenizer then defines the span boundary feeding chunking.

F0001.statement: ChunkingConfig is a frozen dataclass whose __post_init__ enforces invariants: max_tokens positive, overlap_tokens nonnegative and smaller than max_tokens, embedding_limit_tokens positive, max_tokens not exceeding embedding_limit_tokens, nonblank string fields, and a lowercase SHA-256 tokenizer hash.

F0002.statement: ChunkingConfig.version serializes the config fields to sorted-key compact JSON and derives a 'chunkcfg_' prefixed identity via stable_digest, so any config change alters the version.

F0003.statement: Chunk.chunk_id is computed as a stable_digest over document_id, config_version, order, content_text, embedding_text, and each SourceSpan.canonical_value(), producing a content-addressed 'chk_' identifier.

F0004.statement: Chunk.__post_init__ validates that document_id matches 'doc_[0-9a-f]{64}', config_version matches 'chunkcfg_[0-9a-f]{64}', order and embedding_token_count are positive integers, content_text and embedding_text are nonblank, and source_spans is a nonempty tuple of SourceSpan values.

F0005.statement: Chunk.__post_init__ requires source_spans to be in source order by checking (block_number, start_char, end_char) tuples are sorted.

F0006.statement: SourceSpan couples a SourceLocator (from parsers.contracts) with a half-open [start_char, end_char) range and validates start nonnegative and end strictly greater than start.

F0007.statement: SourceSpan.canonical_value() emits sorted-key compact JSON of block_number, end_char, heading_path, page_number, and start_char, and this canonical form feeds chunk_id hashing.

F0008.statement: ChunkingConfig defaults derive tokenizer_model, tokenizer_revision, and tokenizer_sha256 from the shared COHERE_EMBED_ENGLISH_LIGHT_V3 constant, tying chunk identity to tokenizer identity across subsystems.

F0009.statement: DEFAULT_CHUNKING_CONFIG is a module-level default ChunkingConfig instance.

F0010.statement: CohereEmbeddingProvider.embed enforces a maximum of 96 texts per request and raises ProviderError('invalid_request') beyond that.

F0011.statement: CohereEmbeddingProvider.embed maps EmbeddingPurpose.DOCUMENT to input_type 'search_document' and otherwise to 'search_query', and sends truncate='NONE'.

F0012.statement: CohereEmbeddingProvider.embed wraps the SDK call in asyncio.timeout(self.timeout_seconds) and sets RequestOptions max_retries=0, so no automatic retries are performed.

F0013.statement: CohereEmbeddingProvider.embed translates failures into sanitized ProviderError codes: TimeoutError/httpx.TimeoutException to 'timeout', httpx.TransportError to 'unavailable', ApiError 401/403 to 'authentication', 429 to 'rate_limited', >=500 to 'unavailable', other statuses to 'invalid_request', and ValueError/TypeError to 'invalid_response'.

F0014.statement: CohereEmbeddingProvider.embed re-validates the SDK response through the strict _EmbedResponse pydantic model and raises ProviderError('invalid_response') if vector count or per-vector dimension does not match request/configured dimensions.

F0015.statement: open_cohere_embeddings and configured_cohere_embeddings are async context managers that construct and yield a CohereEmbeddingProvider, with configured_cohere_embeddings reading Settings values and refusing live embeddings when cohere_api_key is None.

F0016.statement: configured_cohere_embeddings re-checks that the model 'embed-english-light-v3.0' is paired with 384 dimensions before opening the provider, guarding against mutated Settings instances.

F0017.statement: CohereGenerationProvider adapts the application's GenerationRequest/GenerationResult contract to Cohere's async Chat SDK; it is non-streaming and relies on an injected cohere.AsyncClientV2 whose lifetime it does not own.

F0018.statement: CohereGenerationProvider.generate wraps the SDK chat call in asyncio.timeout and passes RequestOptions with max_retries=0, so retries are not delegated to the SDK; timeouts, transport errors, and ApiError status codes are translated into sanitized ProviderError codes (timeout/unavailable/authentication/rate_limited/invalid_request) with retryable flags for timeout, 429, and 5xx.

F0019.statement: CohereGenerationProvider re-validates the SDK response through the strict _ChatResponse pydantic model and maps finish_reason values: TIMEOUT to a retryable timeout error, ERROR to a retryable unavailable error, TOOL_CALL to invalid_response, and MAX_TOKENS to GenerationFinishReason.MAX_TOKENS; empty text is rejected as invalid_response.

F0020.statement: CohereGenerationProvider computes GenerationUsage cost via _estimate_cost using billed token counts and input/output USD-per-million rates, defaulting to 0.0375 and 0.15, and records latency_ms from perf_counter.

F0021.statement: open_cohere_generation and configured_cohere_generation are async context managers that construct a CohereGenerationProvider; configured_cohere_generation requires settings.cohere_api_key and reads model, timeout, temperature, and price settings from Settings.

F0022.statement: CohereRerankingProvider adapts RerankRequest to Cohere's async rerank SDK call, sends candidate texts as documents with request.top_n, and rejects candidate sets larger than 10,000 with invalid_request.

F0023.statement: CohereRerankingProvider.rerank derives an effective timeout as the minimum of the provider timeout and an optional per-call timeout, and applies the same SDK error-to-ProviderError status mapping pattern as the generation adapter.

F0024.statement: CohereRerankingProvider validates the rerank response invariants: result count must equal request.top_n, indexes must be unique and within candidate bounds, and scores must be sorted descending; otherwise it raises invalid_response.

F0025.statement: CohereRerankingProvider maps each returned SDK index back to request.candidates[index].id, producing RerankItem values with candidate_id, original_index, rank (1-based), and relevance_score, and computes RerankUsage cost from billed search_units and usd_per_search_unit.

F0026.statement: configured_cohere_reranking and configured_cohere_generation docstrings state the live Cohere adapters are opt-in, with ordinary tests and load runs using the fake adapters instead.

F0027.statement: embeddings.py defines the application-owned EmbeddingProvider Protocol (async embed) plus frozen EmbeddingRequest and EmbeddingResult dataclasses; EmbeddingRequest enforces a nonempty tuple of nonblank strings and a DOCUMENT or QUERY purpose, and EmbeddingResult declares an adapter Literal of "fake" or "cohere".

F0028.statement: ProviderError carries a stable ProviderErrorCode Literal (timeout, unavailable, authentication, rate_limited, invalid_request, invalid_response) and a retryable flag, and its docstring states provider response bodies or headers must never be exposed.

F0029.statement: Both Cohere providers import an injected client type from cohere but receive the client as a constructor parameter, so the SDK client lifetime is owned by the caller rather than the provider; the module does not itself import a factory for client creation.

F0030.statement: The generation and reranking adapters share a deliberate error-sanitization convention: caught SDK exceptions are re-raised as ProviderError from None, discarding the original exception context so response bodies and headers are not surfaced.

F0031.statement: It is uncertain whether any runtime application code selects between the fake and Cohere providers via the configured_* context managers, since the supplied excerpts show the factory helpers but no caller wiring.

F0032.statement: It is uncertain whether the generation provider's temperature and timeout validation constraints, or the rerank cost fields, are exercised by any orchestration layer, since no calling subsystem is present in the supplied excerpts.

F0033.statement: The providers package defines application-owned async Protocol contracts — GenerationProvider.generate (S0009), RerankingProvider.rerank (S0010), and an embeddings contract referenced by FakeEmbeddingProvider (S0008) — so callers depend on protocol types rather than provider SDKs.

F0034.statement: FakeEmbeddingProvider.embed, FakeRerankingProvider.rerank, and FakeGenerationProvider.generate are asynchronous coroutines, matching the async Protocol signatures they implement.

F0035.statement: FakeEmbeddingProvider.embed derives each vector deterministically from a SHAKE-256 digest over a canonical JSON of model, dimensions, request.purpose, and text, then normalizes it, so vectors are stable across instances and batch composition but similar text does not yield similar vectors.

F0036.statement: FakeRerankingProvider.rerank scores each candidate as the fraction of distinct case-folded query terms present in the candidate text, sorts by descending score with input order as tie-break, and truncates to request.top_n.

F0037.statement: FakeGenerationProvider.generate returns a synthetic 'Synthetic response {fingerprint}' text with finish_reason COMPLETE, where the fingerprint is the first 16 hex chars of a SHA-256 over model, max_output_tokens, and the ordered (role, content) message pairs.

F0038.statement: All three fake providers report zero usage: EmbeddingUsage/RerankUsage/GenerationUsage with billed_* at 0 and estimated_cost_usd of Decimal(0), so the fake family implies no cost, consistent with the module docstring's 'no network or credential dependencies'.

F0039.statement: The Generation contract is validated at construction: GenerationMessage requires a nonblank content and a MessageRole, GenerationRequest requires a nonempty tuple of messages including at least one USER message and a positive integer max_output_tokens, and GenerationResult requires nonblank text/model and an adapter of literal 'fake' or 'cohere'.

F0040.statement: GenerationUsage and RerankUsage/EmbeddingUsage model reported tokens or search units separately from billed quantities, latency, and estimated cost, and GenerationResult.__post_init__ rejects non-finite or negative numeric usage values.

F0041.statement: estimate_embedding_cost returns None (not zero) when either billed_input_tokens or usd_per_million_tokens is None, distinguishing unknown cost from zero cost; the computation uses the Decimal type rather than float.

F0042.statement: RerankRequest enforces unique candidate IDs and 1 <= top_n <= candidate count, and RerankItem validates original_index >= 0, rank >= 1, and a finite relevance_score, so the reranking boundary rejects malformed ordering before any provider call.

F0043.statement: tokenization.py provides checksum-pinned local tokenizer provisioning: COHERE_EMBED_ENGLISH_LIGHT_V3 binds model 'embed-english-light-v3.0' to a revision and sha256, SUPPORTED_ASSETS is keyed by model name, and configured_tokenizer_asset raises TokenizerSetupError when settings.cohere_embed_model is absent from SUPPORTED_ASSETS.

F0044.statement: load_local_tokenizer verifies file_sha256 of the local tokenizer file against the pinned asset sha256 and raises TokenizerLoadError if the file is missing or the checksum mismatches; the module docstring frames this as verification without contacting Cohere.

F0045.statement: provision_tokenizer avoids overwriting: it returns a TokenizerProvisionResult(downloaded=False) if a verified file already exists, otherwise fetches via the TokenizerFetcher Protocol, verifies the downloaded checksum, writes to a temporary file with fsync, and publishes atomically via os.link, resolving FileExistsError by re-verifying the raced file.

F0046.statement: provision_tokenizer requires settings.cohere_api_key to be present before invoking the Cohere SDK-based fetch path (provision_configured_tokenizer), and sanitizes non-TokenizerSetupError exceptions from the SDK into a generic TokenizerSetupError without exposing credentials.

F0047.statement: The TextTokenizer Protocol declares tokenize(text) -> tuple[TokenSpan, ...], and LocalTextTokenizer implements it by zipping Hugging Face encoding.ids with encoding.offsets and rejecting any span whose end_char is not greater than start_char, defining the tokenizer boundary used by deterministic chunking.

F0048.statement: The GenerationProvider Protocol comment states that grounding and citations belong to a later ('Day 18') scope, so this contract is the text-generation boundary only and does not itself own grounding or citation behavior.

F0049.statement: CohereGenerationProvider.generate(GenerationRequest) is the async entry point that sends a non-streaming request to Cohere's /v2/chat with the configured model, messages, max_tokens, temperature=0.0, and stream=False, then returns a GenerationResult; tests exercise it via an httpx MockTransport (S0013).

F0050.statement: CohereGenerationProvider.__init__ validates constructor configuration and raises ValueError for blank model, non-positive/non-finite timeout, out-of-range or non-finite temperature, and negative or NaN token rates, before any request is made (S0013).

F0051.statement: The provider maps provider finish_reason values independently of content: COMPLETE and STOP_SEQUENCE map to GenerationFinishReason.COMPLETE, MAX_TOKENS to MAX_TOKENS, while TIMEOUT, ERROR, and TOOL_CALL raise ProviderError with codes timeout, unavailable, and invalid_response respectively (S0013).

F0052.statement: HTTP error statuses from Cohere are translated into sanitized ProviderError codes (400 invalid_request; 401/403/498 authentication; 429 rate_limited; 500/503 unavailable) whose retryable flag varies by code, with the provider suppressing the original exception context and performing no retries (calls == 1) (S0013).

F0053.statement: Malformed Cohere responses—empty body, empty content, whitespace-only text, thinking-only content, unknown finish reason, or invalid usage values—raise ProviderError with match 'invalid_response' (S0013).

F0054.statement: Transport and parse failures from the SDK are translated to ProviderError codes by exception type: httpx.ReadTimeout -> timeout, httpx.ConnectError -> unavailable, and ValueError -> invalid_response (S0013).

F0055.statement: CohereGenerationProvider applies a total per-request timeout (timeout_seconds) via an asyncio wait, raising ProviderError('timeout') and cancelling the underlying SDK call, while caller-initiated task cancellation propagates as asyncio.CancelledError (S0013).

F0056.statement: open_cohere_generation is an async context manager factory that constructs a Cohere AsyncClientV2, rejects a blank API key with ValueError('API key'), and closes the SDK client (__aexit__ awaited) on exit (S0013).

F0057.statement: configured_cohere_generation reads Settings (COHERE_API_KEY and COHERE_GENERATION_MODEL env vars), raises ValueError('COHERE_API_KEY') when credentials are missing, and produces a provider whose model and per-million-token rates (input 0.0375, output 0.15 Decimal) come from configuration (S0013).

F0058.statement: GenerationUsage is populated by Cohere's usage block: input/output tokens come from tokens, billed_input/output come from billed_units, latency_ms is measured from perf_counter deltas, and estimated_cost_usd plus per-million rates are Decimal-derived; when the provider omits usage these fields are None (S0013).

F0059.statement: The generation contracts are strict dataclasses: GenerationMessage rejects an unknown role string and blank/whitespace content; GenerationRequest requires a non-empty tuple of GenerationMessage with at least one user message and a positive non-bool integer max_tokens; GenerationResult rejects empty text/model, unknown finish_reason, negative token counts, and non-finite latency_ms (S0014).

F0060.statement: FakeGenerationProvider implements the GenerationProvider protocol deterministically: identical requests produce equal GenerationResults, and no prompt text (e.g. 'Private') appears in the output text, which begins with 'Synthetic response ' (S0014).

F0061.statement: FakeGenerationProvider returns zero billing (billed_input_tokens=0, billed_output_tokens=0, estimated_cost_usd=0) and None token counts and latency, with model 'fake-generation-v1' and adapter 'fake'; distinct request content or max_tokens yields distinct response texts (S0014).

F0062.statement: Both the live Cohere adapter and the fake adapter satisfy the same GenerationProvider contract (message roles, request/result/usage shapes), so callers can substitute one for the other without changing request/result handling (S0013, S0014).

F0063.statement: The generation providers perform synchronous request/response chat (stream=False) rather than streaming; there is no evidence in these tests of a streaming channel or incremental token delivery (S0013).

F0064.statement: CohereGenerationProvider can be constructed directly with an injected client and model for transport-error and configuration tests, separate from the factory helpers open_cohere_generation and configured_cohere_generation that manage SDK lifecycle and settings (S0013).
